newsitem.title: USA: FHP net aided by administrative savings.
newsitem.headline: FHP net aided by administrative savings.

text.p: FHP International Corp., ahead of its $2.1 billion acquisition by PacifiCare Health Systems Inc., Thursday reported higher second quarter earnings.
The health care services company said the earnings improvement resulted from administrative savings primarily from the company's fiscal 1996 restructuring programme.

On Aug. 4, 1996, FHP agreed to be acquired by PacifiCare Health Systems. The combined company will be the nation's fifth largest HMO and have nearly 4 million commercial and Medicare members in 15 states and Guam.
Closing of the transaction is expected in mid-February.
Earnings for the second quarter ended Dec. 31, 1995 rose to $24.9 million, or 42 cents a share, from $13.9 million, or 24 cents a share.
Revenues rose to $1.11 billion from $1.01 billion.
For the six months, earnings rose to $48.5 million, or 82 cents a share, from $27.8 million, or 48 cents a share.
Revenues rose to $2.21 billion from $2.02 billion.
FHP stock was up 37.5 cents at $35 in midday trading on the Nasdaq system.
